explanation: Test whether retaining the acquired bottle neck motor geometry across successful hover, tuck, carry, braking and placement avoids the observed later contact loss. Temporal evidence supports this intervention, not a unique root cause.

Embed V010 geometry/planning directly in one Task(BaseTask) module. Retain its probe/lift/hover acquisition-only running floor, then freeze the successful-hover reference once at tuck. All later hand feedback shares a fixed signed floor with reversible bounded extra closure. Keep it protected throughout place; opening begins only after sustained measured target-table handoff.

S03 V010 fails during close. This first intervention preserves its initial geometry and close logic rather than adding an unsupported independent repair. Repeating that failure is a material expected limitation; S02 improvement alone cannot establish paired improvement.

applicability.binding_enforcement: Runtime rejects other case IDs, objects, orientation axes or reference ratios; parent must enforce exact admitted case/model hashes and initialization.

fixed_invariants: Frozen plant, geometry, PD gains/effort/friction, cases, controller, judge and original eight gates; no infrastructure edits.
NoSlip iterations 0 to 3 at physics step 3960; all29 body actions remain SONIC and hands remain original native14 PD.

Right-hand references stay between zero and .65*RIGHT_CLOSED in native hand_ids name order; a shared tick origin caps net reference change at .006 rad per policy tick across callbacks and release/retraction.
No actual data qpos/qvel/time/ctrl writes, external forces, resets, replay state injection or native stepping. Retained private copied-state geometry/IK queries are reference planning only.
Original slip/acceptance anchors, probe and hover qualification, carry-distance/foot-cycle criteria, physical safety gates, final orientation >=.98 and final quiet-support audit remain binding.

target_handoff_criteria.phase: place or release, place_step=lower, after qualified hover liftoff; close/probe/lift support never unlocks
target_handoff_criteria.contact: Measured payload_surface/generated_desk pair normal sum >= .8*object_weight AND desk_supported
target_handoff_criteria.geometry: Actual payload flex base within measured table top XY bounds with .005 m inset; actual flex-vertex bottom relative to table top in [-.003,.006] m
target_handoff_criteria.target: XY object-origin distance <.10 m from BOTH original case target and geometry-projected place_goal
target_handoff_criteria.posture: World-Z dot (object_rotation @ declared orientation_axis) >.985; angular speed <.25 rad/s
target_handoff_criteria.motion: Object linear speed <.04 m/s, root linear speed <.06 m/s, original reached(tick,data)
target_handoff_criteria.dwell: 21 distinct consecutive 50 Hz policy observations; resets on a missed tick or failed observation; no continuity claim between policy observations
target_handoff_criteria.unlock: No finger opening while in place, even at first contact. Unlock only through release transition with certificate; retain frozen tuple for diagnostics.

changes_from_v010: Freeze the successfully acquired hover motor vector once at tuck and project every later callback into a non-ratcheting envelope. The .060 rad extra-closing band is a conservative untested design bound, not an empirically learned optimum.

Use one tick-origin vector to enforce .006 rad net hand slew, including supported release and retraction, instead of allowing multiple callbacks or the release profile to accumulate a larger tick change.
Replace the sticky first-desk-contact shutdown in airborne_grip with tentative-support hold and resumption on contact loss. Require phase, target, actual geometry/contact and dwell before release.
Add diagnostic events for changing missing-role sets, root versus object posture, wrist-relative rotational drift, projected references and target-handoff certificates.
Retain V010 ready_arm, shape_reference, move and observe method ASTs exactly; no independent S03 geometry repair or wrist-trajectory retuning.

frame_and_index_notes: Resolve each motor by hand_ids names, never by an assumed numeric index. The .843 to .625 reference is right_hand_middle_1_joint (middle distal), not index.

design_verification.static_scan: No native step/reset/setState calls; no assignments to actual data/model fields. Retained qpos assignments are to private planning or copied arrays.

parent_tests_required: Fresh original initialization S02 first, then the identical frozen SHA on S03; no replay prefix, state restore, blind sweep or intervening revision. Retain every failure and exact first-breach feedback.

Compare native named motor references across hover->tuck->carry->target_stop->place and all callbacks. Audit fixed floor, reversible extra-closing bound, signed .65 limits, per-tick .006 slew and retained original acceptance anchor.

Inspect per-role forces, all physics-substep contacts, actuator requested/actual torque, object/wrist rotation and drift before1810. Reconstruct force distribution; do not infer a sole cause from changed failure time.

Verify probe/lift table flicker and incidental hand-table contact never issue a target certificate; verify actual target-table support, base geometry, object axis, dwell reset and support-loss handling in release.

Require original-init all43ctrl continuous replay, independent SONIC29/native14 PD/contact/geometry audit, force reconstruction, full video decode/keyframe review, lineage/content deduplication, all eight gates and original last200-physics-sample settle acceptance.

Keep S03 close failure explicit. Paired improvement requires fresh success evidence on both frozen cases; a later airborne improvement alone is insufficient. Cup regression remains a separate parent task with its existing scoped baseline.
limits: No new trajectory, success, causal learning, generalization, complete-skill qualification or automatic deployment approval.

Signed closing bounds preserve reference geometry but do not guarantee actual force, opposing contact, wrench feasibility or wrist alignment; extra closure can increase force and safety rejection remains authoritative.

The .060 rad band, .8 weight support threshold and geometric/motion tolerances are unvalidated. Conservative support readiness or slew-limited release can time out or fail even after a better airborne grasp.
Handoff dwell sees policy observations, not every physics substep. Parent must audit the substep history; final settle is still decided independently by the original judge.
Actual mesh-base/table checks use the admitted table top XY bounding rectangle and flex vertices, not a general support-polygon proof; geometric contact alone never certifies load transfer.
Support loss during release causes a visible stop, not a dynamically validated recovery. No regrasp rescue, wrist redesign or initial S03 acquisition repair is claimed.
